title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1967-10-22
lineage: SBD > Rm > Cass > DAT (Sony TCD-D8) > CDR (Tascam CDRW700) > EAC (Plextor 48/24/48 - Secure Mode) > Samplitude v7.0 > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a high‑energy 1967 set with smoking Lovelight, New Potato Caboose and the debut That's It For The Other One suite.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised for its raw psychedelic fire—standout performances of Lovelight, New Potato Caboose and the first full "That's It" suite dominate.  The soundboard source is generally clear for the era, though a few reviewers note a dodgy start and occasional drop‑outs.  Overall the music outweighs the minor technical flaws, delivering an exhilarating early‑Dead experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for performance (many 5‑star reviews) and mostly positive comments on sound quality; only occasional mentions of minor drop‑outs, giving a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well balanced for a 1967 tape; some reviewers mention a dodgy beginning and occasional drop‑offs, but most find the audio excellent for its age.

standout_songs: That's It For The Other One suite
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early psychedelic set that builds momentum, featuring fast blues numbers and soaring jams; the debut "That's It" suite serves as a climactic centerpiece.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Firey solo work praised, tone described as perfect; occasional minor stumble on changes noted but overall dominant lead guitar.
band_member_comments.Phil: Strong bass counterpoint and building confidence; highlighted for tight interaction with Jerry during New Potato and other jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s powerful vocals on Lovelight and bluesy delivery on "It Hurts Me Too" praised; original early lyrics in "That's It" noted as a highlight.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ described as haunting/funeralistic at times, occasionally not fully gelled with the jam but adds atmospheric depth.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s first recorded appearance; reviewers note Bill and Mickey working smoothly together, providing solid rhythmic foundation.
